chapter: The House That Jazz Built and Homestead childhood
title: Picnics, grandmother's travels and her mother's second marriage
summary: She visited the valley towns as a youngster; her mother married again and her brother uses the name Williams.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Let me ask another question that is prompted by looking at Earl Hines -- the book about Earl Hines, and that is, he mentions a band that his father had, called the Eureka Brass Band which used to play for picnics in Kennywood Park. Do you have any recollections --

Well, I wouldn't know about that but the name rings a bell. I probably was too young to know, but I certainly would remember Kennywood Park because that's where the school picnics were held every year. But there was a small park in Homestead that we used to attend when I was quite

young which finally closed and then we began to have the picnics in Kennywood Park which was nearer to Duquesne than to Homestead. We used to have to ride out to Kennywood where we could walk to the Homestead Park. So in my early days that's where we had our picnics and there's a possibility that my Uncle Jess and his band might have played at the Homestead picnics. I don't recall, but if they had a band, that would have been the band.

See as a youngster, my grandmother, my mother's mother she used to travel a lot. She was always going to some of these small areas around Homestead in the coal mining area -- Connelisville, Pennsylvania and Uniontown. There were coal mines there and also other mills. She had friends all over. I know that what would happen to me in the summer when school was out, I was always sent to the country for a vacation and I spent a lot of time with so-called -- they weren't uncles and aunts, real uncle and aunts, but they were friends of hers and she would, you know, she would come and spend a little time there. But I thought I was a world traveler, you know, when I was

young. I lived and visited all the little towns in the so-called valley there. So that might be one of the reasons why I don't recall too much about Homestead on any continuous basis because I was in and out of Homestead quite a bit when I was young.
Yeah. Did your mother marry again after your father died?
Yes, she married again and I have a brother who is an offspring of her second husband -- Paul, he lives in Braddock now, he's three years younger than I am and he --
Was Williams the surname of the second husband?
No, no, White, but he uses the name of Williams, my brother uses the name of Williams.
